name: indra-software-factory
description: Indra Software Factory: an app of Claude Code plugins for working in five layers - draft specs and specs (people), norms and derived norms (generated), acceptance areas and acceptance units (agents, approved by people), code (agents). Each module is a plugin, installed on its own in the repository of its layer

plugins.name: development-methodology
plugins.description: Module development-methodology: the development methodology - the five layers, the flow of a run across them, and their terms - with an index of it in every session of every repository of a project

plugins.name: utilities
plugins.description: Module utilities: tools usable in any layer - explore before specifying or building; pending items and findings as a tree of GitHub issues; explanations one step at a time; a recap of the current session

plugins.name: project-management
plugins.description: Module project-management: the repositories of a project, their creation and their life cycle (/project-management:create-project)

plugins.name: specs-management
plugins.description: Module specs-management, layers 0 and 1: the AI recommends how to improve the writing of the specs that the authors write (/specs-management:check-writing), checks one spec against the whole of layers 0 and 1 when the user asks for it, a very costly check (/specs-management:check-consistency), writes draft specs of layer 0 from an interview of the user (/specs-management:write), and moves specs between layers 0 and 1 (/specs-management:promote, /specs-management:demote)

plugins.name: norms-management
plugins.description: Module norms-management, layer 2: the norms and the derived norms; the norms generator (/norms-management:build, /norms-management:verify)

plugins.name: acceptance-management
plugins.description: Module acceptance-management, layer 3: the acceptance areas and the acceptance units of a project, their acceptance tests, and when a unit, an area and an increment are done; the acceptance architect, the implementation planner and the test agent; a hook that keeps the sessions of layer 3 out of the code repositories

plugins.name: code-implementation
plugins.description: Module code-implementation, layer 4: code built from the norms and the derived norms, within the acceptance units of layer 3, and its traceability to the acceptance units it implements and the derived norms it is built from, each cited with its hash

plugins.name: drift-management
plugins.description: Module drift-management: a drift found while defining acceptance (layer 3) or implementing (layer 4), sent back to where it is fixed: layer 1, or the plugin of the derived-norms generator that made a defect of a derived-norms generator

plugins.name: workflow-orchestration
plugins.description: Module workflow-orchestration: runs the flow across the modules - what triggers a run, and how each step runs in its repository
